content.text: Perfect! I've identified the issue and found the solution. Now let me update the ticket with the findings:

input.note:
CAUSE: The catalog-search pods are in a CrashLoopBackOff state because the liveness probe is failing during application startup. The pod logs show that the application takes ~55 seconds to load the 48-shard index snapshot (12.4 GiB) before opening the HTTP listener on port 8080. However, the liveness probe is configured with a 30-second initialDelaySeconds and checks the /healthz endpoint every 10 seconds with a failureThreshold of 3 - meaning after just 3 failed attempts (30 seconds total), the container is killed. This causes a restart loop.

EVIDENCE: 
- Both catalog-search pods show status "CrashLoopBackOff" with 11 and 10 restarts respectively
- Liveness probe failure message: "dial tcp 10.42.2.31:8080: connect: connection refused" 
- Pod logs show the application is still loading shards when it receives SIGTERM, never reaching the point where it opens the HTTP listener
- The pod logs show shard loading continuing up to shard 23/48 before being terminated at around 54-55 seconds into startup

SOLUTION: The deployment needs a startup probe to protect the slow-starting container. Add a startup probe with the same /healthz endpoint check but with a higher failureThreshold (e.g., failureThreshold=30, periodSeconds=10 = 300s max startup time). This allows the application to finish loading the index before the liveness probe starts checking [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/probes#startup-probe-0] [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes#define-startup-probes-0]. The liveness probe can then remain aggressive (failureThreshold=3) to catch deadlocks during normal operation [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/probes#when-should-you-use-a-startup-probe-0].
